_meta.purpose: Pest records for the crops the bundled visual model can see, plus the arthropod pests the health screening can flag. Scientific names are standard accepted names; every record is stored UNVERIFIED until a named published source is attached to that individual record.
_meta.safety_rule: No pesticide dose is recorded here. A dose belongs to a specific product label and is stored only in treatments.json with a label reference.

pests.name: Two-spotted spider mite
pests.appearance: Minute eight-legged mites, usually pale green to yellow-green with two dark spots on the back; barely visible without a hand lens. Fine silk webbing on the leaf underside.
pests.feeding_behavior: Pierces leaf cells and sucks out the contents, leaving the leaf stippled and bronzed. Colonies build up on the underside of leaves and spread upward.
pests.damage_symptoms: Fine pale stippling over the leaf surface that merges into yellow-bronze patches; fine webbing on leaf undersides and shoot tips; leaves dry out and drop. Worst in hot dry weather.
pests.life_stages: Egg, larva, protonymph, deutonymph, adult. Development is very fast in hot dry conditions, so populations can explode within days.
pests.prevention: Keep plants well watered and avoid water stress; maintain humidity; encourage predatory mites and other natural enemies; avoid excess nitrogen; inspect leaf undersides regularly.
pests.management: Strong water jets to dislodge colonies; remove and destroy heavily infested leaves; acaricides are used where permitted, and repeated application is often needed because eggs survive sprays. Rotate modes of action to slow resistance.

symptoms.text: fine pale stippling on the upper leaf surface
fine silk webbing on leaf undersides and shoot tips
leaves bronzing, drying and dropping in hot dry weather

pests.name: Asian citrus psyllid
pests.appearance: Small brown mottled psyllid about 3-4 mm long that holds its wings roof-like over the body; nymphs are yellowish and produce white waxy honeydew.
pests.feeding_behavior: Feeds on new flush growth; while feeding it transmits the bacterium that causes citrus greening (huanglongbing).
pests.damage_symptoms: Distorted and stunted new shoots; heavy white waxy secretions and sooty mould; notched or twisted young leaves. The most serious impact is virus-free transmission of huanglongbing rather than direct feeding damage.
pests.life_stages: Egg, five nymphal instars, adult. Eggs are laid in the tips of new flush.
pests.prevention: Inspect new flush regularly; manage psyllid populations on surrounding citrus and Murraya (curry leaf); use certified disease-free planting stock.
pests.management: Vector control is the practical management; systemic insecticides are used where permitted. Remove and destroy confirmed huanglongbing-infected trees and report suspected cases to the state horticulture department.

symptoms.text: white waxy secretions and sooty mould on shoots

pests.name: Sweetpotato whitefly
pests.appearance: Tiny white moth-like insects about 1 mm long that rise in a cloud when the plant is disturbed; nymphs are flat oval scales on the leaf underside.
pests.feeding_behavior: Sucks sap from the phloem and excretes honeydew; vector of many plant viruses including begomoviruses.
pests.damage_symptoms: Yellowing and distortion of leaves; sticky honeydew with black sooty mould; virus transmission causing severe stunting and leaf curling.
pests.prevention: Use insect-proof nets in nurseries, reflective mulches, yellow sticky traps for monitoring; remove crop debris; manage weeds that host the insect.
pests.management: Traps and nets, conservation of natural enemies (Encarsia, Eretmocerus parasitoids, predators), then selective insecticides where permitted. Rotate modes of action because resistance develops quickly.

symptoms.text: clouds of tiny white insects when the plant is disturbed
sticky honeydew with black sooty mould on leaves
yellowing and distortion of leaves with stunting

pests.name: Cotton bollworm
pests.appearance: Caterpillar up to about 40 mm, variable colour from green and brown to nearly black, with pale longitudinal stripes and a light band behind the head.
pests.feeding_behavior: Larvae bore into buds, flowers, pods and bolls, feeding on developing seed and tissue. One larva can damage several fruits.
pests.damage_symptoms: Round bore holes with frass at the entry point; hollowed bolls, pods or fruit; flowers and squares shed; secondary rot in damaged tissue.
pests.life_stages: Egg, six larval instars, pupa (in soil), adult moth.
pests.prevention: Deep summer ploughing to destroy pupae; timely sowing; trap crops such as marigold; pheromone traps for monitoring; conserve natural enemies; avoid excessive nitrogen.
pests.management: Pheromone traps, hand picking of larvae, biological agents including Bacillus thuringiensis and HaNPV where suited, and host-plant resistance. Insecticides are used on economic-threshold counts per the local recommendation, not on sight alone.

symptoms.text: round bore holes with frass on fruit or bolls
hollowed fruit and shed buds or flowers

pests.name: Brown planthopper
pests.appearance: Small brown planthopper about 4-5 mm; adults occur in two wing forms, and nymphs are white to brown and crowd around the base of the tillers.
pests.feeding_behavior: Sucks sap at the base of the rice tiller; heavy feeding causes the classic patchy wilting known as hopperburn.
pests.damage_symptoms: Plants dry out and turn brown in irregular patches within a field, often in a circular pattern that spreads; honeydew and sooty mould at the base; severe lodging.
pests.life_stages: Egg, five nymphal instars, adult (brachypterous and macropterous).
pests.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen and continuous flooding; leave gaps between crop cycles; grow resistant varieties; conserve spiders and mirid bugs.
pests.management: Encourage natural enemies, drain the field temporarily, and apply insecticides only directed at the base of the tillers where the hoppers sit. Follow the state recommendation for economic thresholds.

symptoms.text: patches of plants drying and turning brown in the field
honeydew and sooty mould at the base of the tillers

pests.name: Aphids
pests.scientific_name: Aphididae (multiple species, e.g. Myzus persicae, Aphis gossypii)
pests.appearance: Small soft-bodied insects, usually green, black, brown or pinkish, clustered in dense groups on new growth and the underside of leaves.
pests.feeding_behavior: Sucks sap from young shoots and leaves; excretes honeydew and transmits many plant viruses.
pests.damage_symptoms: Curled distorted new growth; sticky honeydew with sooty mould; colonies clustered on shoot tips; virus transmission causing mottling and stunting.
pests.life_stages: Nymph and adult (winged and wingless forms); colonies can be all-female and reproduce without mating in warm conditions.
pests.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen, manage weeds, encourage ladybirds, hoverflies, lacewings and parasitoid wasps, and monitor shoot tips weekly.
pests.management: Strong water jets to dislodge colonies, remove affected shoot tips, and conserve natural enemies. Insecticides are a last resort because they also kill the predators that keep aphids in check.

symptoms.text: colonies of small soft insects clustered on shoot tips
sticky honeydew with black sooty mould

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.appearance: Soft oval insects covered in white powdery wax, often with waxy filaments around the edge; they hide in leaf joints, stem crevices, under pot rims and on roots.
pests.feeding_behavior: Sucks sap from stems, leaf joints and roots; excretes honeydew.
pests.damage_symptoms: White cottony clusters in leaf axils and on stems; yellowing and stunted growth; sticky honeydew with black sooty mould; in pots, cottony white masses at the drainage holes.
pests.life_stages: Egg (in a waxy sac), three nymphal instars (crawlers), adult.
pests.prevention: Inspect new plants before bringing them in; isolate new plants for a few weeks; avoid overwatering and excess nitrogen; keep plants unstressed.
pests.management: Remove by hand with a cotton bud dipped in alcohol; strong water jets; wash pots; mealybug destroyer beetles and parasitoid wasps where suited. Systemic insecticides exist but are not a first step indoors.

symptoms.text: white cottony clusters in leaf axils and on stems
sticky honeydew with black sooty mould
